subject: Renewal: commit reprice & staged forgiveness
messages:
From: Olivia Barnes <olivia@clearviewretail.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@clearviewretail.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning and ask for flexibility

Hi David,

We’re starting our renewal conversations for Clearview Retail. Our usage this year spiked during the holiday rollout and the team is asking whether Redwood can provide a short-term price hold while we migrate some workloads to a deduped pipeline. Specifically: 

- Can we get a price hold for 90 days from the renewal effective date?
- Is there any one-time overage forgiveness or credit for the quarter where we exceeded our commit by ~27%?
- We’re open to a higher committed tier if there’s a staged uplift/discount schedule, but procurement needs the invoice cadence aligned to our fiscal calendar.

CC’ing Tom (Procurement) — he’ll lead the PO/invoice side.

Thanks,
Olivia Barnes
Head of Infrastructure
Clearview Retail

---
Attachment: usage_summary_q4_2026.csv (csv)
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@clearviewretail.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@clearviewretail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning and ask for flexibility

Thanks for the context, Olivia — appreciate the heads-up. I ran the numbers with ops and product. High level proposal we can move quickly on: 

1) Short-term price hold: 90-day price hold at your current committed rate effective at renewal (no retroactive change).

2) Staged uplift (commit swap): If you move to a 20% higher commit for 12 months we can tier the discounts: 0–3 months = existing rate (price hold), 4–6 months = 5% discount on over-commit usage, 7–12 months = 8% discount and a one-time onboarding credit.

3) Overage forgiveness: For the past quarter we can apply a one-time credit equal to 50% of the overage dollars as a goodwill concession, contingent on signing the renewed term within 30 days.

4) Invoice alignment: We can offer invoice timing options (monthly or quarterly) but need to confirm payment term. I’ve attached a draft term sheet with two invoice cadence options and an example True-Up schedule.

I’ve looped in Marissa for approvals on the concession level and to formalize the term sheet. Tom — let us know the preferred invoice cadence and whether DocuSign is fine for PO-level signoff.

Next steps: If this looks directionally OK I’ll prepare a formal amendment and route for approval.

Best,
David
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: Clearview_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v3.pdf (pdf)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Olivia Barnes <olivia@clearviewretail.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@clearviewretail.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning and ask for flexibility

David — thanks for the draft. A few internal notes / guardrails before you hand this to legal: 

- The 50% overage credit is OK as a one-time concession for Strategic customers, but we should cap total concessions to $120k for this FY unless the renewal goes multi-year.
- Add a hard cap language on the price hold: applies only to standard SKU list prices; additional premium features are excluded.
- Require a 30-day sign window to qualify for goodwill credit (document the date triggers).

If Clearview agrees I’ll pre-clear with finance and legal and return a final amendment template. Also cc’ing Monica for ops onboarding notes (cache warming, prefix caching) — she’ll coordinate the migration schedule that enables the commit uplift.

Marissa Cole
VP, Sales — North America
Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@clearviewretail.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@clearviewretail.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Sep 2027 08:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning and ask for flexibility — operational notes

Hi Olivia / team — quick operational check on the uplift path: 

- If you opt for the 20% commit increase we recommend a phased traffic migration across three stages (week 0, week 4, week 12) to allow KV cache priming. Expect a ~10–15% token cost improvement after stage 2.
- For the price hold period we’ll enable prefix caching on the busiest routes and prioritize your fleet for burst capacity during the 90-day window.
- On invoicing: we can align billing to quarter boundaries but require a signed SOW/amendment before we shift invoice dates. Ops will need 10 business days notice to change billing cadence.

I’ll prepare a short ops checklist to attach to the amendment.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@clearviewretail.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olivia Barnes <olivia@clearviewretail.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 02 Oct 2027 11:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: commit reprice & staged forgiveness

David / Marissa — we reviewed the term sheet internally. Clearview is comfortable with the 90-day price hold and the 50% one-time overage credit (we accept the $120k cap). Two asks before we sign: 

1) Can the onboarding credit be applied to the first invoice of the new term (helps our cashflow)?
2) We’d like the invoice cadence moved to quarter-aligned billing (starting the next fiscal quarter). If you can draft the amendment with those items we’ll route for PO signature.

If that works, please send DocuSign and we’ll aim to return a signed PO within 7 business days.

Thanks — Tom Reynolds
Procurement Director
Clearview Retail
